en.title: Maximum Length Where Every Fixed-Length Window Is Below the Threshold
en.description:
Given an array of positive integers and k, find the maximum length L such that every contiguous subarray of length L has a sum strictly less than k. If no positive length works, output 0.

This site has made the standard input and output explicit; any range not given by the source is marked as this site's protocol.
en.input: The first line contains n k, and the second line contains n positive integers. 1≤n≤200000, 1≤a[i]≤10⁹, 1≤k≤10¹⁸.
en.explanation: Example 1: the two windows of length 3 have sums 6 and 7, both less than 8; length 4 gives 10, which fails, so the answer is 3. Example 2: the only element sums to 9, which is not strictly less, so the answer is 0. Example 3: the whole array sums to 3, less than 10, so the maximum length is 3.
hints: First find the length B of the shortest subarray whose sum is at least k; the answer is B−1. If none exists, the answer is n. Because all numbers are positive, two pointers can find the shortest qualifying window in linear time.
